Screenshots

Every image is a real capture from the playable build, not a mockup: tools/run-scenario.sh drives the game with real input events inside a nested headless compositor and screenshots the live viewport. Seed 20250912, Fighter, Tokyo Night unless the caption says otherwise.

Where it stands

Signed off for release. All three independent judges approved the build after eight rounds: a first-time player, a rogue-like veteran, and a quality engineer trying to break it.

The stopping bar, set before the last rounds and met in full: no blockers; nothing that loses player progress or reports a success it did not earn; all three judges signing off; and the release gate green across repeated runs. Fourteen remaining minor issues are written up in the patch list rather than held against the release.

RoundFindingsBlockersSign-offsWhat it turned on
15040 of 3A fully green suite had caught none of it
23930 of 3Save and resume rebuilt
32410 of 3Dungeon lighting; curses given a real cost
43520 of 3Rose: the lighting fix had flattened the themes
52512 of 3Gate made deterministic; colour restored
62602 of 3Loose drops persist; tooling made honest
71511 of 3Projectiles hit walls; gate reproducible
81903 of 3Offer boards keep their identity

The rounds that rose did so because a fix opened an adjacent hole. One shape recurred throughout: state regenerated when a run resumes instead of restored.

The last bug was the most valuable. Packaging the final build caught a script that compiles in the editor and in every test, but not in the exported binary, where it broke the run manager outright. A fully green suite of 1485 tests never touches the exported build. The package smoke test does, and it refused to ship.

Verified on real Omarchy

Beyond the headless rendering tier, the build is now installed and exercised inside a genuine Omarchy 4.0.3 virtual machine: unattended install, the Debian package installed, the game launched in the machine's own Hyprland session, and the system theme switched repeatedly to confirm the dungeon recolours live without a restart.

Decisions locked

  • Theme source is colors.toml from ~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme; resolver mirrors upstream.
  • Wallpaper: Omarchy shell symlink (video-aware) and otter-wallpaper state file, with a config fallback for a single fixed wallpaper.
  • otter-theme colours read through theme.conf, so a stock theme with any wallpaper works, not just wallpaper-generated palettes.
  • Environment-only tinting, live retint mid-level, per-room palette variants.
  • A seed fixes the rolls, not the run: theme, wallpaper and the track playing are generation inputs too, so the same seed under another theme is another dungeon. The run file records all of them.
  • Quit is resumable at room granularity; separate Abandon Run.
  • Omarchy Radio bundled with credits; spectrum drives lights and gen.
  • All testing in nested headless sway; real Omarchy in a libvirt VM later.

Up next

  • Finish the chest variants the design calls for: cursed chests and the Oligarch's buy-anything contract.
  • Balance pass driven by simulation, then game feel: hit-stop, shake and readability under every shipped theme.
  • Accessibility: colour-blind glyphs on rarity and status, reduced flash, hold-to-toggle.
  • Three independent playtesters, then a targeted fix pass.
  • Final check inside a real Omarchy virtual machine.

Log

Times are UTC. Committed entries are stamped from the commit history; the top entry is work in the tree that has not been committed yet.

2026-09-12 19:35

Released. All three judges signed off. Final verification on a quiet tree: 1485 tests green across three consecutive runs with no leaked nodes, compile and lint clean over 452 scripts, and both Debian packages rebuilt, extracted and run. Fourteen remaining minors are written up as a patch list.

2026-09-12 19:20

A bug that only existed in the shipped build. An unqualified call compiled in the editor and in every test but not in the exported binary, where it broke the run manager. Caught by the package smoke test, which runs the real binary with no desktop theme present.

2026-09-12 18:14

The last two integrity bugs. Death is permanent again: the save used to outlive the player for over a second, so closing the window in that window resurrected the run. And a stat thief now repays its debt on any despawn, not only when killed, so quitting after a bite no longer costs a point forever.

2026-09-12 17:00

Round eight: offer boards keep their identity. Leaving an altar and returning used to deal three fresh cards, a better reroll than the one the game charges gold for. Boards now persist the cards themselves.

2026-09-12 16:10

Round seven: the gate can be trusted. Concurrent test runs had been fighting over one save directory. Ten concurrent runs now come back green. Projectiles also stopped passing through walls.

2026-09-12 12:48

Round five: flakiness traced to the game, not the tests. An item effect decided where its gold went by counting listeners on a global signal.

2026-09-12 10:35

Round four: the dungeon got its colour back. Theme identity restored inside the lighting model, with real light sources.

2026-09-12 04:23

First playtest round. Three testers found 50 issues and 4 blockers in a build whose entire test suite was green.

2026-09-11 20:09

Project started. Godot project, Omarchy and otter-shell integration, and a harness that renders screenshots in a nested headless compositor so testing never touches the real session.
